tools.name: check_url
tools.description: Check any public URL RIGHT NOW: is it up, HTTP status, response time in ms. Works without an API key (rate limit 10/hour per IP). For continuous monitoring with alerts, use create_monitor.

tools.name: list_monitors
tools.description: List all monitors on the account: current up/down status, kind, target, interval, last check. Optionally filter by tag.

tools.name: get_monitor
tools.description: Full detail for one monitor: status, config, 24h latency percentiles and trend (http/tcp), SLA budget if a target is set. Heartbeat monitors include their ping_url and ping_email.

tools.name: create_monitor
tools.description: Create a monitor. kind=http (needs url), tcp (target "host:port"), tls (target host[:port] — cert-expiry watch), domain (target — registration-expiry via RDAP), dns (target + rtype A/AAAA/MX/... , optional expect_value), heartbeat (dead-man’s switch for cron jobs/agent loops: needs name; response in

tools.name: update_monitor
tools.description: PATCH any monitor field: name, url, target, interval, expect, keyword, slow_ms, grace, cron, tags, sla_target, renotify, channels (alert routing)... Pause with {"status":"paused"}, resume with {"status":"new"}. Empty string clears optional fields.

tools.name: delete_monitor
tools.description: Permanently delete a monitor and all its check history, events and rollups. Cannot be undone.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: Downtime incidents (ongoing and resolved) across all monitors: start, duration, cause, acknowledgement, notes.

tools.name: ack_incident
tools.description: Mark an ongoing incident as "someone is on it" — pauses still-down reminder alerts for that monitor until recovery. Set un=true to un-acknowledge (re-arms reminders).

tools.name: add_incident_note
tools.description: Attach/replace a note (max 500 chars) on an incident. Notes publish with the incident on public status pages, their JSON and the Atom feed. Empty string clears.

tools.name: list_channels
tools.description: Alert delivery channels on the account (email / webhook / Discord / Slack / ntfy / Telegram), their verification state and delivery health.

tools.name: get_status_page
tools.description: Machine-readable state of any public Watchpup status page by slug: per-monitor status, uptime, incidents last 30d. No API key needed.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: Who am I: account email, monitor count/limit, plan limits. Good first call to verify the API key works.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "create_monitor" is 759 chars, far longer than this server's median (150). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

evidence.snippet: Create a monitor. kind=http (needs url), tcp (target "host:port"), tls (target host[:port] — cert-expiry watch), domain (target — registration-expiry via RDAP),…

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_url, list_channels, get_account · Private data: check_url, get_status_page, get_account · Public sink: add_incident_note, list_channels, get_account · Destructive: delete_monitor.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_url, list_channels, get_account · Private data: check_url, get_status_page, get_account · Public sink: add_incident_note, list_channels, get_account · Destructive: delete_monitor

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
